integrity: Same-side resolving neighborhoods force all but at most one deleted-matching pair to meet every resolving set. Equality forces a one-per-pair transversal. Such transversals resolve all vertex pairs for n at least four. For k at least two every minimum transversal dominates; for k equal to one domination is equivalent to selecting at least two vertices from each bipartition class. The basis counts follow by direct binomial enumeration, and a standalone verifier checks the definitions exhaustively on finite ranges.
scientific_limitations: The uniform classification is stated for crown graphs with n at least five.
The small cases n=3 and n=4 have exceptional distance-1 behavior and are not included.
Identifying-code and locating-total-domination variants are not covered.
Finite exhaustive verification over 5 <= n <= 8 and k in {1,2,3} is corroborative only.
A differently named or non-indexed classical locating-dominating result on crown graphs could exist despite targeted searches.
title: Distance-k locating-dominating bases of crown graphs
